STYLE GUIDE
YOKAI FIGHTERS STYLE GUIDE: STORY-CARD TEXT

TONE
T1. Mischievous folklore with a melancholy edge, never horror. Nothing gory, cruel, demonic or frightening: no blood, screams, corpses, souls devoured, darkness swallowing anything. (Source: rules.md S1; GDD §2.1; vault Tone#The tone line)
T2. Yokai are tricksters and lonely spirits, not monsters. A yokai that wins walks away or goes back to what it was doing; it never hurts Ryo for pleasure and never gloats over him. (Source: rules.md S1; vault Tone#The tone line, Story#Wake-up cards)
T3. Melancholy is small and specific: something owed, borrowed, waiting or left behind. Never doom, despair or the end of the world. (Source: vault Tone#Do and don't examples)
T4. The merchant and the Tanuki share one voice: cheerful, generous and quietly hungry. It compliments what it wants, teases Ryo as "little exorcist" and never shouts, threatens or sounds evil. The unease comes from how pleasant it is. (Source: vault Tone#Voice: the merchant and the Tanuki; Characters#The merchant and the Tanuki)
T5. Wit is dry and in period. No modern slang, memes, fourth-wall jokes, exclamation-mark shouting or capitals for emphasis. (Source: vault Tone#Do and don't examples ("LOL, nice talismans, bro"; "MINE now, fool!"))
T6. Ryo is earnest and stubborn. He apologises to the yokai he binds; he never boasts, threatens, vows revenge or jokes at a yokai's expense. (Source: vault Tone#Voice: Ryo; GDD §2.2)

VOCABULARY AND LORE
V1. Ryo is an apprentice exorcist who binds yokai: an ink stroke seals the yokai into a paper talisman. He never kills, slays, destroys, defeats-and-captures or hunts them, and he does not "collect" them: collecting is the Tanuki's word. Ryo fights with talismans, never a sword or a gun. (Source: GDD §2.2; vault Story#Talismans, Tone#Do and don't examples, Characters#Ryo)
V2. Never call a yokai a monster, demon, beast or creature of evil. "Oni" is a yokai's name, not an insult. (Source: rules.md S1; vault Characters#The yokai as a group, Tone#Voice: Ryo)
V3. Only the 5-week build's cast exists: Ryo, Master Sōen (she), the merchant who is the Tanuki, Kitsune, Oni, Kappa, and the elders Nine-Tailed Kitsune, Elder Oni and Elder Kappa. Never the stretch-goal names Jorōgumo, Tengu, Tetsu, Kaede or Yūrei, and never supers, Acts 2 or 3 or the Yūrei gauntlet. (Source: rules.md G1-G5; vault Characters#Not in the 5-week build)
V4. The world is one rural Japanese province at the end of autumn, folded into the Tanuki's illusion: dusk, lantern light, things about to end. Each fighter has a home: Kitsune the bamboo grove at dusk, Oni the snowbound shrine gate, Kappa the lantern riverbank, the Tanuki a tea house whose paper screens flicker between seasons. No spring blossom, castles, cities, neon or night-time dread. (Source: rules.md V9; GDD §2.1; vault Tone#The tone line, Story#The illusion loop)
V5. Each yokai keeps its folklore and voice: the Kitsune (she) teases and slips away, white fox mask with red markings, tails, foxfire; the Oni (it) is proud and blunt with an iron club; the Kappa (it) is formal, stubborn and polite, bows and carries water in the dish on its head. (Source: vault Characters#Kitsune, #Oni, #Kappa; Tone#Voice: yokai)
V6. Fixed lines are quoted word for word when a card uses them: "Forgive me, {yokai}. I'll set your spirit free." (every binding), "That {move} of yours... I'd love one." (row 4), "I said I'd set you free." (ending), and Master Sōen's rule "name the debt". (Source: rules.md S3; AM2; vault Tone#Voice: Ryo)
V7. Story facts hold: after a loss Ryo wakes at the province's edge and his talismans are blank, except that a run that reached row 6 or further leaves one talisman faintly inked. The merchant is revealed as the Tanuki only at the boss node. (Source: rules.md M3, S3; vault Story#Talismans, Story#Wake-up cards)

FORM AND LENGTH
F1. A story card is one or two sentences and at most 280 characters. An elder intro card is exactly one sentence of at most 140 characters. (Source: rules.md S2, Y3; vault Tone#Card form, Story#Elder intro cards)
F2. Present tense, plain words, one concrete image from the game's world: a lantern, a paper screen, a tail, a teacup, an ink stroke, a red seal, snow on a shrine gate. (Source: vault Tone#Card form)
F3. Names that depend on the player's run come through placeholders: {yokai} for the yokai and {move} for a move. A card never hard-codes a move the player may not own. No other placeholders. (Source: rules.md S4; vault Tone#Card form)
F4. No system words. A card does not say health, HP, damage, frames, level, Lv, meter, XP, unlock or roguelite, and shows no game numbers; it says what a person standing there would see. (Source: vault Tone#Card form; rules.md A12 (numbers live behind the frame-data toggle))
F5. Plain card text only, as it appears in a story card's "text" field: no title, heading, bullet points, Markdown, emoji, speaker label or stage directions. (Source: data/story/*.json (story_card text field); vault Story#Card schedule)
